chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man looks into a business and sees nothing in it (no profit), let him turn to another.
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if a business venture is not profitable according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *istiqra'* (continuing in beneficial matters) within commercial jurisprudence. It advises merchants to abandon ventures that lack clear benefit (*manfa'a*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on rational utility and avoiding waste (*israf*) in trade. This ruling underscores the ethical obligation to ensure that business activities align with both economic prudence and spiritual well-being.
